text:
Design, settled 19 November 2026 after reading the acceptance path, backup and recovery.

1. The record is a pure function of the accepted release: kind (bids or archive), title, description, creators, keywords, data types, licence, identifiers. BIDS: Name, Authors, Keywords, License and DatasetDOI from dataset_description.json; description from the root README (capped); data types from the coverage summary. Archive: the same fields from archive_description.json, which the interpretation already holds. Anything unreadable is recorded as missing; building a record never fails.
2. It is a projection, not part of the interpretation. Adding it to the interpretation would change every existing BIDS release's reading and force a re-assessment of each.
3. Written only inside the acceptance transaction: NativeRepository.accept is the single caller of Catalog.accept, computes the record from the candidate's manifest and descriptor bytes, and passes it in. No lazy write on read: recovery hashes every table into its scientific digest, so a table that changes on reads would break restore verification.
4. Older releases have no row. A read computes the record on demand without storing it. An operator command (repository rebuild-catalog STORAGE) backfills with the same function, so live and rebuilt records are identical and no release or manifest identifier changes.
5. Disclosure follows ADR 002: discovery shows only the steward's label, as today. Every record field needs ReadMetadata on that exact release. So the two levels in criterion 4 are: label by Discover, record by ReadMetadata.
6. Storage: new table release_catalog (release_id primary key, dataset_id, record jsonb) in migration V017; an in-memory map in the reference catalog. pg_dump backups carry it.
7. Wiring: a small ReleaseDescriber port given to NativeRepository; DatasetInterpreter's module supplies it. HTTP: GET /v1/datasets/{d}/releases/{r}/catalog. The release payload is unchanged, so the upgrade-compatibility allow-list is untouched.
